headline: The squeeze finished its lap around the globe overnight — Taiwan +9%, Korea +7% — and bitcoin still printed a lower low at 60,338.
summary: What changed since yesterday is geography, not substance. The US gamma-unwind got exported: TWII +9.0%, KS11 +7.0% to 5,039, N225 +4.0%, with the ETF mirrors EWT +18.0% and EWY +10.1% closing the gap to a session Asia never traded. TSM +14.1%, MU +19.0%, ASML +9.3%, SMH +15.0%, SOXX +13.6%, NVDA +31.5% to 165.05. Volatility surrendered: VIX -25.8% to 26.62, VIX3M -17.6% to 25.50. And the front end finally broke the other way — 2y -13bp to 4.63, 5y -15bp to 4.71, 10y -12bp to 4.92, 10y real -11bp to 2.77. On paper that is the whole bull case: lower discount rate, lower vol, global catch-up.

The instruments that trade continuously refused to ratify it. Bitcoin is 60,338, -1.3% on the session and -24.6% on the month, at the 4.6th percentile of its 52-week range; ETH -27.1% and SOL -29.3% over a month. Equities squeezed 5-7% and crypto made a new low — that is a liquidity signature, not a sentiment one. The dollar did the same: DXY 104.27, 100th percentile, z=1.16 with acceleration +0.64; EURUSD 1.0912 and GBPUSD 1.3037 both at the 0th percentile; USDCAD z=1.45 acc +1.14; USDBRL +17.4% on the month with z=4.75 and acceleration +3.52. And credit never moved. HY OAS 3.76 (+24bp on the day, +49bp on the month), CCC 14.02 (+95bp/+365bp over 1m/3m), BBB 1.22, IG 0.98 — all four at the 100th percentile of the past year. VIX/VIX3M is still 1.0439, backwardated at the 71st percentile. Risk regime improved two points to -19; credit & vol and dollar are both pinned at -56.

The macro underneath is a disinflation shock crashing into a front end that hasn't been told. Brent -6.8% to 86.29 and -26.1% on the month, WTI 79.75 (-22.8%), gasoline -25.9%, DBC with a 1m z of -3.01 and acceleration -2.44. Breakevens have capitulated: 5-year 2.15 (-33bp, z=-1.58), 10-year 2.13 (-21bp), both the 0th percentile of the year. Yet the 3-month bill sits at 4.32% against an effective funds rate of 3.88%, 3m10y has flattened 23bp in a week to 55bp, and the 10-year real yield is 2.77%, 85th percentile and 22% above its 200-day. That is passive tightening into collapsing nominal growth, with core CPI still turning up (+30bp, z=0.93) and the inflation composite at 63. Copper -15.0% on the month, FCX -23.7%, CAT -20.2% (z=-2.29), AUDUSD z=-2.15, AUDJPY -4.1%: the cycle-sensitive complex is not buying the tech bounce either.

So own the dispersion, not the beta. The winners of a cheaper-barrel, stronger-dollar world keep working: India (BSESN +12.7% 1m, z=3.01, INDA rel. strength +18.1%, USDINR -1.9%), health care (XLV rel. strength +5.3%/+8.7%, IBB up-trend), and the defensive cash machines — MCD +11.2% on the month (z=2.05), TGT +10.9%, COST +9.6%, UPS +9.0%, WMT +8.1%, HD +8.2%. The losers keep losing: Brazil (BVSP -19.6%, EWZ -31.3% with acceleration -3.75), Argentina -22.6%, REMX -12.6%, NLR -11.5%. One genuine new development: precious metals have stopped being margin collateral — gold +3.2% to 3,629.6 and silver +3.4%, GDX +6.4%, GDXJ +7.0%, with real yields finally falling. Gold sits at the 6th percentile of its 52-week range and the gold/silver ratio at 85.6 is the 99.8th percentile. That's where the forced-seller mispricing now lives.

good.text: Volatility broke hard: VIX -25.8% to 26.62, VIX3M -17.6% to 25.50, VIX/VIX3M -10.0% — the acute phase of the deleveraging is over for now.
The front end finally helped: 2y -13bp to 4.63, 5y -15bp to 4.71, 10y -12bp to 4.92, 10y real -11bp to 2.77, MOVE -5.1% to 100.9. Belly z-scores of -0.9 to -1.0 mean the rally is real, not noise.
Asia completed the catch-up without new damage: TWII +9.0%, KOSPI +7.0% to 5,039, N225 +4.0%, EWT +18.0%, EWY +10.1%, TSM +14.1%, ASML +9.3%.
Energy disinflation is a real-income tailwind: Brent -26.1% and gasoline -25.9% on the month, DBC 1m z=-3.01, 5y breakevens at 2.15 — the 0th percentile.
Precious metals have exited forced-liquidation: gold +3.2%, silver +3.4%, GDX +6.4%, GDXJ +7.0%, with GDX/gold +3.2% and acceleration turning positive.
Defensive compounders and health care keep making relative highs: MCD +11.2% 1m (z=2.05), TGT +10.9%, COST +9.6%, UPS +9.0%, WMT +8.1%; XLP rel. strength +9.7% over 3m, XLV +8.7%.

bad.text: Credit flatly refused to confirm: HY OAS 3.76 (+24bp d, +49bp m), CCC 14.02 (+95bp m, +365bp 3m), BBB 1.22, IG 0.98 — all at the 100th percentile of the 52-week range while equities squeezed 5%.
Crypto made a new low into the equity squeeze: BTC 60,338 (-1.3%, 4.6th percentile, -24.6% 1m), ETH -27.1% 1m, SOL -29.3%, MSTR -42.2%. The marginal liquidity buyer is gone.

The dollar is still the wrecking ball and it is accelerating: DXY 104.27 at the 100th percentile (z=1.16, acc +0.64), EURUSD and GBPUSD at the 0th percentile, USDCAD acc +1.14, USDBRL +17.4% 1m with acc +3.52, CEW -2.3%.

Passive tightening persists: 3m bill 4.32% versus 3.88% effective funds, 3m10y flattened 23bp in a week to 55bp, 10y real yield 2.77% at the 85th percentile and 22% above its 200-day, 30y mortgage 7.28%.
The cyclical core is still breaking, faster than the index: copper -15.0% 1m (z=-2.35), FCX -23.7%, CAT -20.2% (z=-2.29), COPX -17.7%, XME -11.7%, AUDJPY -4.1%, XOP 1m acceleration -1.96.

Hedges got trimmed, not replaced: VIX/VIX3M still backwardated at 1.0439 (71st percentile) while SKEW fell 7.5% on the month to the 33rd percentile — low crash demand on top of unhealed plumbing (bank reserves -1.4% 1m, net liquidity -0.8%).

trades.name: Short junk, own duration
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF: spreads at 100th pctile, equities don't care
trades.expr: Short HYG against a dollar-matched long in IEF; or buy 3-month HYG 74 puts financed by selling 80 calls if you prefer convexity.
trades.thesis: High-yield is the only market that never retraced. HY OAS widened 24bp on the same day SPX rose 4.7%, CCC is 14.02 after +365bp in three months, and IG/BBB/HY/CCC all sit at the 100th percentile of the 52-week range. With breakevens at the 0th percentile and oil -26% on the month, nominal revenue for levered issuers is falling while funding costs are not. Duration is the hedge: the belly is rallying (5y -15bp) on the same disinflation that kills junk cash flows.
trades.trigger: HY OAS +24bp on the day and +49bp on the month (z=1.63); HYG/IEF -1.1% on the month (z=-0.97) despite HYG +0.2%.
trades.stop: HY OAS back inside 3.40 and CCC below 13.00 with HYG/IEF reclaiming its 200-day — that would mean the squeeze was a real re-risking.

trades.name: Fade the beta squeeze
trades.line: Short SPHB vs long SPLV after a +8.6% one-day ratio pop
trades.expr: Short SPHB against long SPLV, dollar-neutral; add to the short on any further 3%+ up-day in the ratio.
trades.thesis: High-beta/low-vol ripped 8.6% in a session and is still -8.1% on the month (z=-1.32) at the 20th percentile of the year. Short-covering rallies in the exact names that were margin-called narrow breadth rather than broaden it — RSP/SPY fell 2.0% and IWM/SPY 1.1% on the up-day. With the dollar at the 100th percentile and credit at its widest of the year, leverage does not get re-financed here; it gets re-sold.
trades.trigger: SPHB +9.5%, ARKK +8.0%, IPO +8.6% in one session while HY spreads widened and BTC fell; MTUM 1m z=-2.13.
trades.stop: Ratio up 7% from entry, or VIX sustained under 20 with HY OAS inside 3.40.
trades.target: Round-trip the squeeze: ratio back to the lows, roughly 10% of relative performance.

trades.name: Short MSTR into the bounce
trades.line: MSTR +8.5% while BTC printed a new low at 60,338
trades.expr: Short MSTR outright, or buy 2-month 75 puts. Size small — realized vol is enormous.
trades.thesis: Bitcoin is the cleanest liquidity read in the digest and it went the wrong way: -1.3% to 60,338, 4.6th percentile, -24.6% on the month, while QQQ rose 7.0%. MSTR is the levered claim on that reflexivity — down 42.2% in a month, and its +8.5% session is sympathy with equity beta, not inflows. Net liquidity -0.8% on the month and bank reserves -1.4% say the marginal bid doesn't come back this quarter.
trades.trigger: BTC and ETH both lower on the overnight session (-1.3%/-1.5%) against a 4-7% US equity squeeze; COIN +6.7% off a -33.9% month; IBIT 7th percentile.
trades.stop: BTC closes above 68,000, or MSTR above 102 — that breaks the lower-high sequence.
trades.target: MSTR 62-65 on BTC testing the low 50s.

trades.name: Long silver vs gold
trades.line: Gold/silver 85.6 at the 99.8th pctile — own the cheap metal
trades.expr: Long silver (futures or SLV-equivalent) against a dollar-matched short in GLD, roughly 1:1 notional.
trades.thesis: The gold/silver ratio at 85.6 is the 99.8th percentile of the year after +14.7% in a month, driven by silver being sold as collateral in the deleveraging (-21.0% 1m, 1.9th percentile) rather than by industrial fundamentals. Both metals turned up together this session, and with the 10-year real yield off 11bp and the belly rallying, the precious complex has a tailwind for the first time in three months. Mean reversion in the ratio is the lower-variance way to own that.
trades.trigger: Silver +3.4% and gold +3.2% on the day, GDXJ +7.0%, GDX/gold +3.2% with acceleration +0.88; AU_AG 1m z=+2.13.
trades.stop: Gold/silver above 92 — that means the liquidation is still running and silver is still collateral.
trades.target: Ratio back to 75-77, roughly 11-13% of relative gain.

trades.name: Oil importer over squeezed silicon
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWT after Taiwan's +18% catch-up day
trades.expr: Long INDA against short EWT, dollar-neutral.
trades.thesis: India is the purest beneficiary of a -26% monthly move in Brent plus a softening USDINR (-1.9% 1m, z=-1.95): BSESN +12.7% on the month with z=3.01 and relative strength +18.6%. Taiwan is the opposite trade — a semiconductor beta proxy that is still -15.9% on the month after a single +18.0% gap-fill session, with EWT relative strength -11.5%/-10.0% and TWII 1m z=-2.38. Fade the mechanical catch-up, keep the fundamental winner.
trades.trigger: EWT +18.0% and TWII +9.0% in one overnight session purely to close the gap to NVDA; INDA -1.4% on the day, giving a better entry on the long leg.
trades.stop: Brent back above 100, or INDA/EWT down 8% from entry.
trades.target: 12% of relative performance as Taiwan gives back half the gap-fill.

trades.name: Health care over semis
trades.line: Long XLV vs short SMH: +8.7% vs -11.3% 3m relative strength
trades.expr: Long XLV against short SMH at 1:1 notional; use SOXX if SMH borrow is tight.
trades.thesis: The only sector in an uptrend with positive relative strength on both horizons is health care: XLV +5.3% 1m and +8.7% 3m vs the S&P, 12% above its 200-day, with IBB in an uptrend and LLY +7.3% on the month. Semis are the opposite — SMH 12.4% below its 200-day, relative strength -8.2%/-11.3%, 1m z=-1.58 even after a 15% session. In a tape where credit is at the widest of the year and the dollar is at the highs, inelastic cash flow beats cyclical capex.
trades.trigger: SMH +15.0% in a single squeeze session restores the short at a far better level; XLV +1.2%, IBB +4.6%, with XLV's relative-strength state still 'up' while SMH's is 'rolling over'.
trades.stop: SMH reclaims its 200-day (roughly +12% from here) with SMH/SPY above the 50th percentile.

trades.name: Gas over oil
trades.line: Long natgas vs short WTI: +34% vs -23% on the month
trades.expr: Long front natural gas futures against a short in WTI crude, equal notional. Keep it small — this is the highest-variance idea on the sheet.
trades.thesis: The commodity complex is in freefall with DBC's 1m z at -3.01 and acceleration -2.44, but natural gas is the single exception: +34.2% on the month, +13.5% on the week, turning up with acceleration z=+1.73 on winter demand and power load. Crude is the opposite — WTI -5.0% on the day and -22.8% on the month with acceleration -2.22, OPEC supply and weak global demand (copper -15%, AUDUSD z=-2.15) both pressing. Own the structurally tight molecule against the structurally loose one instead of taking outright commodity beta.
trades.trigger: NATGAS +3.9% on the same session WTI fell 5.0% and Brent 6.8%; gasoline cracks collapsing (-25.9% 1m) confirms the demand side of the crude short.
trades.stop: A warm-weather break below 3.10 in gas, or crude reclaiming 88 on a supply event.
trades.target: 20% of relative performance over the heating season.
